clean_source_blocks.text: There are now 380 confirmed cases of Ebola in DR Congo, far lower than initial estimates of suspected cases, writes Fergus Walsh.

Fall in official Ebola numbers appears to be good news but it's not that simple What is Ebola and why is stopping the latest outbreak so difficult? Two people shot dead amid Kenya protests against US Ebola quarantine centre plan Two shot dead during Kenya protests over US Ebola centre plan. Video, 00:00:54Two shot dead during Kenya protests over US Ebola centre plan How health workers in DR Congo are treating Ebola and staying safe Two possible Ebola cases in Brazil ruled out as patients test negative Three Ebola vaccines in development amid growing outbreak fears Five patients recover from Ebola in DR Congo and leave hospital Brazil monitors two patients for possible Ebola infection Ebola spread in DR Congo 'deeply alarming', MSF warns Kenya court halts opening of US Ebola quarantine facility in the country

The latest Ebola figures from the Democratic Republic of Congo appear to offer some hope after the number of cases was dramatically scaled back. At one point the authorities were talking of more than 1,000 suspected cases and nearly 250 suspected deaths. They are now reporting around 380 confirmed cases in DR Congo, including 60 deaths, plus another 15 confirmed cases and one death in neighbouring Uganda. However, the key difference is that the authorities are now talking about confirmed, rather than suspected, cases as before. So it would be a mistake to assume that the fall in numbers means the outbreak is suddenly less dangerous. The decline reflects better data, as laboratories were able to rule out many patients who had fever but were suffering from other conditions such as malaria which is common in DR Congo.

original_article.research:
[Lähde: BBC World]
The latest Ebola figures from the Democratic Republic of Congo appear to offer some hope after the number of cases was dramatically scaled back.

At one point the authorities were talking of more than 1,000 suspected cases and nearly 250 suspected deaths.

They are now reporting around 380 confirmed cases in DR Congo, including 60 deaths, plus another 15 confirmed cases and one death in neighbouring Uganda.

However, the key difference is that the authorities are now talking about confirmed, rather than suspected, cases as before.

So it would be a mistake to assume that the fall in numbers means the outbreak is suddenly less dangerous.

The decline reflects better data, as laboratories were able to rule out many patients who had fever but were suffering from other conditions such as malaria which is common in DR Congo.

The director general of the World Health Organization (WHO) Dr Tedros Adhanom Ghebreyesus has said the outbreak had a "big head start" but response teams are now "catching up".

However, one of the biggest concerns remains contact tracing. Only about 45% of people in direct contact with an Ebola patient are currently being followed up, partly because the epicentre of the latest outbreak is in an area hit by conflict.

The WHO says at least 90% of contacts must be traced to bring an outbreak under control.

Another challenge is mistrust among some communities. An Ebola burial team was reportedly attacked this week in South Kivu province, forcing responders to abandon a coffin and raising fears of further transmission.

Traditional burial practices often involve washing and touching the body, and funerals typically draw large crowds - all high risk for Ebola, which is spread from one person to another by contact with infected bodily fluids.

Tedros said building trust with communities was critical to bringing the outbreak under control.

The Ebola outbreak is concentrated in three provinces of eastern DR Congo, an area roughly the size of the United Kingdom, much of it rural, remote and difficult to reach.

It is also unfolding in one of the most volatile regions in Africa, with many armed groups operating.

The latest outbreak is caused by the Bundibugyo species of Ebola, which has only occurred twice before. Because it is much rarer than other types of Ebola, there is no vaccine or proven treatment, although various teams are trying to develop them.

payload.title: Kongon ebolaluvut pienenivät, mutta riski ei ole väistynyt
payload.summary: Kongon demokraattisen tasavallan ebolatilanteessa viralliset tapausluvut ovat laskeneet selvästi aiemmista epäiltyjen tapausten arvioista. Muutos kertoo ennen kaikkea tarkentuneesta laboratoriotiedosta, ei siitä, että epidemia olisi äkillisesti muuttunut vaarattomaksi.
payload.content:
Kongon demokraattisessa tasavallassa on nyt raportoitu noin 380 vahvistettua ebolatapausta ja 60 kuolemaa, mikä on selvästi vähemmän kuin aiemmat arviot yli 1 000 epäillystä tapauksesta ja lähes 250 epäillystä kuolemasta. Lukujen lasku näyttää ensi silmäyksellä rohkaisevalta, mutta se johtuu ennen kaikkea siitä, että viranomaiset puhuvat nyt vahvistetuista tapauksista eivätkä aiemmista epäilyistä.

## Vahvistetut luvut muuttivat kuvaa

Aiemmat arviot perustuivat epäiltyihin tapauksiin, joissa potilailla oli kuumetta tai muita oireita, jotka saattoivat sopia ebolaan. Kun laboratorioissa on pystytty tutkimaan tapauksia tarkemmin, monilta potilailta on voitu sulkea ebola pois.

Tämä on pienentänyt virallista tapausmäärää, mutta ei tarkoita, että tauti olisi saatu hallintaan. Osa potilaista oli sairastanut muita alueella yleisiä tauteja, kuten malariaa. Kongon demokraattisessa tasavallassa tällaiset sairaudet voivat aiheuttaa oireita, jotka alkuvaiheessa muistuttavat ebolaa ja vaikeuttavat nopeaa tilannekuvaa.

Naapurimaa Ugandassa on lisäksi raportoitu 15 vahvistettua ebolatapausta ja yksi kuolema. Se kertoo, että tilannetta seurataan myös Kongon demokraattisen tasavallan rajojen ulkopuolella.

## Epidemian torjunta pysyy vaikeana

Ebolan torjunta vaatii nopeaa tunnistamista, potilaiden eristämistä ja terveydenhuollon työntekijöiden suojaamista. Lähdetietojen mukaan Kongon demokraattisessa tasavallassa epidemiaa ovat vaikeuttaneet myös konfliktit, epäluulo hoitokeskuksia kohtaan ja levottomuudet.

Aiemmissa tilanteeseen liittyvissä raporteissa on kerrottu muun muassa väkijoukkojen häirinneen ebolan hoitokeskuksia, Punaisen Ristin vapaaehtoisten kuolleen epäiltyyn ebolaan ja terveysjärjestöjen varoittaneen taudin sekä konfliktin vaarallisesta yhteisvaikutuksesta. Lisäksi taudin riskiä on kuvattu erittäin korkeaksi Kongon demokraattisessa tasavallassa.

## Seuraavaksi ratkaisee tarkka seuranta

Siksi nykyisiä lukuja on tulkittava varovasti. Tarkentuneet tiedot ovat hyvä asia, koska ne auttavat kohdentamaan hoitoa ja torjuntatoimia paremmin. Samalla vahvistettujen tapausten ja kuolemien määrä osoittaa, että ebola on yhä vakava uhka alueella.
summary_bullets: Kongon demokraattisessa tasavallassa on raportoitu noin 380 vahvistettua ebolatapausta ja 60 kuolemaa.
Aiemmat arviot olivat suurempia, koska ne perustuivat epäiltyihin eivätkä vahvistettuihin tapauksiin.
Laboratoriotestit ovat sulkeneet pois monia tapauksia, joissa oireet johtuivat muista sairauksista, kuten malariasta.
